scope.policy: sequential retries only; concurrent hedging is not implemented or claimed
scope.gate: disabled by default and enabled explicitly through ServiceConfigParseOptions or SharedChannelOptions
scope.wire_boundary: the per-attempt receive timer cancels local I/O without shortening or renewing the logical RPC grpc-timeout
scope.terminal_boundary: the overall RPC deadline returns error.Timeout; exhausted per-attempt timers return CANCELLED with retry perAttemptRecvTimeout exceeded

reference.implementation: grpc-core C++ retry service config and legacy retry filter
observed_contract: a positive perAttemptRecvTimeout permits an empty retryableStatusCodes list
each physical attempt owns a timer and normal throttling and backoff still apply
the last timed attempt returns CANCELLED containing retry perAttemptRecvTimeout exceeded

implementation.parser: ServiceConfig.parseWithOptions owns the optional protobuf Duration only when enable_per_attempt_recv_timeout is true; the default parser ignores the field
implementation.retry_driver: a fresh attempt deadline is derived after each backoff, timeout records one throttle failure, emits CANCEL, and starts the next attempt sequentially
implementation.ordinary_channel: connection readiness and aggregate I/O use the attempt deadline; the wire timeout is recomputed from the original absolute RPC deadline; timed aggregate state retires the connection
implementation.shared_channel: each unary Job owns separate attempt and RPC deadlines; the worker uses the RPC deadline for HEADERS, the attempt deadline for local stream lifetime, and an operation deadline for the current output
implementation.final_response: exhaustion synthesizes one owned transport-free CANCELLED UnaryResponse with the grpc-core status text

native_cases: ordinary Channel timeout then ABORTED then OK with previous-attempt metadata 1 and 2
ordinary Channel final timed attempt returns CANCELLED without retryableStatusCodes
SharedChannel timeout then OK while reusing one HTTP/2 connection
a 50 ms overall deadline wins a configured 200 ms per-attempt timer
every timed attempt is observed by the server as RST_STREAM(CANCEL)
wire grpc-timeout remains above the 200 ms attempt timer for a 2 s RPC and below it for the 50 ms overall-deadline case
